item.title: What redistricting means for Tennessee voters
item.description: What happens when Congressional district lines are redrawn, splitting neighbors and grouping them with people far away
item.dc:creator: Ally J. Levine, Bianca Flowers, David Hood-Nuño
item.content:encoded: It’s a political fault line that leaves neighbors onboth sides with less say. 9th District5th District The street outside Tammy Jo O'Neal's home has become a political boundary with big implications. The city of Memphis used to sit almost entirely in one congressional district. The new map splits O'Neal from neighbors across the street, each now belonging to districts with voters halfway across the state who have different needs and interests. O'Neal sees the new map as more than a split block. “There's this divide that's happening in our lives,not just in our districts.” District 5 District 9 Tammy Jo O’Neal sits for a portrait on the front porch of their home on Elzey Ave in Memphis, Tennessee, US, July 29, 2026. REUTERS/Seth Herald A citydivided By Bianca Flowers , David Hood-Nuño and Ally J. Levine Published Oct. 17, 2026 6:00 a.m. EDT What happens when congressional district lines are redrawn, splitting neighbors and grouping them with people far away Four years before the Memphis redistricting, Republicans used a similar strategy in drawing new maps for Nashville. They split the city, which had voted overwhelmingly Democratic for roughly 70 years, into three broader districts where Republicans can now easily prevail. Battles over redistricting have long been intertwined with racism and political power, particularly in southern states like Tennessee. Sixty-four years ago, a federal court found Tennessee diluted voting power in urban areas where majority Black voters lived and ordered the legislature to redraw its congressional districts. For decades, the Voting Rights Act of 1965 was a powerful tool for Black voters, particularly in the South, to challenge discrimination and protect political power among people of color to elect representatives who would advocate for their communities. The act significantly increased Black and Hispanic representation in Congress by curtailing certain redistricting practices, including splitting people of color among many districts or concentrating them in some districts to limit their impact in others. But those protections have been steadily weakened. In 2013, when Democrat Barack Obama was president, the Supreme Court’s decision on the Alabama case Shelby County v. Holder gutted a provision requiring federal approval before states change voting laws or political maps. In April, the court narrowed the Voting Rights Act further in Louisiana v. Callais , making it harder to challenge new maps that dilute the voting power of communities of color. The court essentially required such challenges to prove that districts were drawn intentionally to discriminate on the basis of race, and not for other reasons. Republicans argue their redistricting in Tennessee and elsewhere is about party politics, not race. They point out that Democrats regularly redraw districts in states they control to give their party easier election wins. Democrats have done the same in California, for example, said Steve Hickey, chair of the Republican Party in Williamson County, a popular suburban area south of Nashville. “This is part of a bigger game being played nationally, and I don’t think it’s fair to say that this was done to gut” the Voting Rights Act, he said. Redistricting in the United States is generally controlled by state legislatures, which adjust voter maps after the once-a-decade census. Both parties have historically used the process to help their candidates win future elections. In 2025, at the urging of President Donald Trump, Texas launched an unusual mid-decade redistricting drive as part of a broader Republican push to gain congressional seats in half a dozen states, including Tennessee. Democrats responded with their own partisan redistricting in California and attempts that faltered in other states. Civil rights activists say Tennessee’s congressional districts, all of which currently favor Republicans, are now a testing ground for dismantling voting rights protections across the United States. “This lack of competition spills over and has racial implications,” said John Geer, a political science professor at Vanderbilt University who conducts polling in Tennessee. Reuters sought to quantify the impact of redistricting on the voters of Tennessee, examining public funding, demographics and socioeconomic factors to show why it’s important to residents when a city is split up like this. MemphisDistrict 9Suburbs of NashvilleDistrict 5District 8District 9 Population by race, one dot per person Black residents White residents Other races and ethnicities Memphis has the largest Black population in Tennessee. The city of some 630,000 people is 63% Black. Memphis accounted for 78% of the former District 9’s population, making it the only majority-Black district in the state. Earlier this year, the Tennessee legislature drew new district lines, splitting Memphis and its Black communities into three separate districts. The pieces of the city are now grouped with rural and suburban Tennesseans in districts that reach halfway across the state. Note: “White” and “Black” are non-Hispanic. “Other races and ethnicities” combines Hispanic or Latino residents of any race with the non-Hispanic categories Asian alone, American Indian and Alaska Native alone, Native Hawaiian and Other Pacific Islander alone, Some Other Race alone, and Two or More Races. Sources: US Census Bureau (2020 census redistricting data; TIGER/Line boundaries); Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury (2026 districts); All About Redistricting, Loyola Law School (2022 districts); State of Tennessee and the City of Memphis Engineering Division (city limits); Tennessee Department of Transportation (roads) Reuters spoke to more than 35 redistricting scholars, political analysts, civic leaders, political candidates and voters about the consequences of redistricting for the most vulnerable communities in Tennessee’s two biggest cities. Cities faced the biggest impact because rural areas were already represented by a Republican and continue to be so after the redistricting, albeit in districts with different demographics. Before redistricting, both Nashville and Memphis were overwhelmingly Democratic districts in an otherwise Republican state. In 2024, District 9, including most of Memphis, went 71% for Democrat Steve Cohen. In 2020, Jim Cooper, a Democrat, ran unopposed in Nashville’s District 5, winning more than 99% of votes cast. In 2022, the new District 5 flipped, with the Republican candidate winning 57%. Tennessee’s new maps have combined city, suburban and rural populations that have widely varying needs and political preferences. The residents of Nashville and Memphis, for instance, are far more likely to struggle with poverty, housing, public safety and related issues. Residents there could now struggle to elect Congress members who prioritize policies to address these issues, according to Odessa Kelly, executive director of Stand Up Nashville, a nonprofit community organization that advocates for racial and economic equality. She said Black voters in Nashville no longer felt they had someone to stand up for them in Congress, from federal funding going to the city to critical votes on bills that directly affect city residents. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention developed the Social Vulnerability Index to gauge how well a community can withstand and recover from an emergency, and to identify which communities may need the most support. Shelby County, home to Memphis, ranks among the most vulnerable of Tennessee’s 95 counties on various indicators such as housing cost burden and lack of access to a vehicle. Memphis, Nashville residents rank higher in social vulnerability A US government index compares Tennessee communities on socioeconomic and demographic factors gauging their resilience to unexpected hardships. 25th 50th 75th 100th percentile Lower vulnerability Higher vulnerability Shelby County (Memphis) Minority status Racial or ethnic minority 100 Davidson County (Nashville) Housing and transportation In structures of 10+ units 97 No vehicle available 94 More people than rooms 60 Lives in group quarters 56 Mobile homes 0 Household characteristics Aged 17 and under 97 Single-parent household 96 Speaks English less than well 91 With a disability 9 Aged 65 and over 5 Socioeconomic status Housing cost burdened 100 Unemployed 86 No health insurance 76 Below 150% of poverty 50 No high school diploma (25+) 16 0 Chart showing where Shelby County and Davidson County rank among Tennessee’s 95 counties on 16 measures of the CDC’s Social Vulnerability Index, grouped into four themes, on a scale from the 0 to the 100th percentile with the other 93 counties as faint ticks. Both rank high on most measures — Shelby at the 100th percentile for racial or ethnic minority share and housing cost burden, Davidson at the 100th for apartments in large buildings and for people who speak English less than well. Both drop to the middle or bottom on poverty, the 50th percentile for Shelby and the 23rd for Davidson, and on residents aged 65 and over. Source: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry Social Vulnerability Index 2022 In 2024, just over a third of Tennessee voters picked Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris, and in 2020, Democrats won two congressional seats out of the state’s nine, carrying Nashville and Memphis. Now, every congressional district in Tennessee is considered “safe” for Republicans. Sandi Wells, a self-described “very conservative” voter from Williamson County, just outside Nashville, said it was “kind of odd” to group Memphis in the same district with parts of Williamson County 200 miles away. But she rejected the notion that districts should be drawn to protect Black voting power. “I don’t think we should have districts that are based on race,” she said. “I mean, that’s just ridiculous for anyone to even think that we should have that.” Shane Tinnin, a 52-year-old small business owner who maintains homes in both cities and has voted mostly for Democrats, understands that parties seek political power through redistricting but called the Memphis maps a particularly striking setback for Black political power. “In Nashville, it seemed really more like this is a political move,” he said, noting that it was not a Black-majority city. “When you do it in Memphis, where it’s an even more liberal district, but also a predominantly Black district, it just feels especially egregious to me.” Odessa Kelly, executive director at Stand Up Nashville, points to topics of focus for her and her team at a meeting in July. REUTERS/Seth Herald Volunteers for The Equity Alliance canvass through neighborhoods in Memphis to do “accountability” door knocks to speak with residents about elected officials following the GOP-led effort to redistrict the city. REUTERS/Seth Herald Securing funding Reuters examined how Nashville’s redistricting has impacted community project funding, under which lawmakers can seek federal money for local projects. Previously known as earmarks, community project funds returned to Congress with a more transparent process in fiscal year 2022 after a decade-long moratorium. A Reuters analysis found a dramatic shift in funding for Nashville after the city was split among three districts. Jim Cooper, a Democrat, steered most of the old 5th District’s project funding to Nashville in fiscal years 2022 and 2023. In the years since, only a small share of funding has gone toward projects in the city, including fiscal year 2027 requests still pending before Congress. Funding can vary greatly between representatives. Only John Rose, who currently represents the 6th District, has requested funding among the three members whose districts included Nashville after redistricting. Matt Van Epps and Andy Ogles have not pursued community project funding for their districts at all, arguing against such spending on principle. All three did not provide a comment or did not respond to a request to comment. Total Community Project Funding for districts that include Nashville After FY2023 FY2024 $18 mln $21 mln $2.5 mln Not Nashville $18 mln Nashville Nashville $3 mln $15.5 mln Before Two flow diagrams comparing Community Project Funds before and after redistricting. In the year before, when Nashville sat in a single district, District 5 received $18 million and $15.5 million of it went to Nashville, with $2.5 million going elsewhere. In the year after, with Nashville divided across three districts, Districts 5, 6 and 7 received $21 million between them but only $3 million reached Nashville, while $18 million went to areas outside the city. Note: Data show the total funding for districts that include Nashville. Before the 2022 redistricting, Nashville was contained in District 5. After, it was split between Districts 5, 6 and 7. Source: US Government Accountability Office The shift away from community funding jeopardized future funding for projects like public housing, healthcare centers, buildings for the two historically Black colleges in the city and public transportation in Nashville. For Memphis, a similar decline in earmark funding would be a big loss. Since 2022, District 9 Representative Steve Cohen, a Democrat, pulled in $52.6 million for projects based in Memphis, according to figures published by the US Government Accountability Office and the US House Committee on Appropriations. That’s 83% of all the community project funding for District 9 in that period. District 7 State capitol District 6 State House of Representatives The Tennessee State Capitol building and Legislative Plaza, which is undergoing construction. REUTERS/Seth Herald Another important role for a member of Congress is to act as a middleman between people in their district and the government, helping negotiate the bureaucracy of Washington. When Cooper represented Nashville, he fielded calls about immigration paperwork, passports, Medicare, Social Security checks and more, said Tennessee State Senator Charlane Oliver, who worked as a community liaison and communications staffer in Cooper’s congressional office from 2017 to 2019. “He would show up to the cookout, the fish fry, the parades, the meetings and the galas,” she said. That kind of interaction is harder if the representative does not have a local office. When Nashville was split, only one representative, Mark Green of District 7, kept an office near the center of the city. That office was closed when Van Epps took over the seat in 2025, leaving no offices within the city limits. Constituents in Nashville have to drive 36 miles on average to visit a congressional district office, a Reuters analysis found, compared with less than 10 miles when Cooper represented Nashville, the seat of Davidson County. Average trip to Congressional district office District 5 +39 miles after District 6 +17 mi District 7 +16 mi 0 10 20 30 40 50 miles 9 miles before redistricting A chart of the average driving distance for Nashville residents to their closest congressional district office, shown for each of the three districts the city is now split among. A dark bar common to all three marks the 9-mile average from when Nashville sat in a single district, flagged on the scale as “9 miles before redistricting.” A lighter bar extends past it to each district’s new average: District 5 adds 39 miles, reaching about 47; District 6 adds 17, reaching about 25; and District 7 adds 16, reaching about 24 miles. Note: Data shows the average driving distance for Nashville residents in each district to their closest district office. District 7’s offices are those open under Rep. Matt Van Epps, who won the seat after Mark Green resigned in 2025. Green kept an office in downtown Nashville; which put District 7’s average at 5 miles. That office no longer exists. Source: Reuters analysis of congressional district office locations Van Epps and the other two Republicans running this year in Nashville districts, Johnny Garrett and Charlie Hatcher, did not respond to Reuters requests for interviews for this story. Most city buses don’t operate far enough outside the city to visit a congressional district office in Cookeville, more than an hour’s drive away. Kyle Cook, who works in the public library, said Cooper’s office used to be just upstairs from his own in downtown Nashville. “Now, if I wanted to advocate just as a regular citizen for better busing, I would have to call this office in Cookeville and it’s just not the same kind of relationship,” Cook said. Who speaks for Memphis? Cohen represented Memphis for 19 years but stood down when new maps were passed, saying “these districts were drawn to beat me.” State Representative Justin Pearson, a progressive Democrat, is campaigning to represent the 9th District. Pearson gained national attention in 2023 when he was temporarily expelled from the Tennessee House, for what Republicans described as a breach of decorum when he joined a protest on gun control . Polls show him trailing Brent Taylor, a Republican state senator endorsed by President Donald Trump. But Pearson said Tennessee was “not a lost cause” for Democrats. In an interview with Reuters, Pearson described the Memphis redistricting as “one of the most significant political deprivations of Black political power and accessibility to the ballot since the end of Reconstruction in Tennessee.” Tennessee State Representative Justin Pearson stands for a portrait in the Cooper Young neighborhood in Memphis. REUTERS/Seth Herald Taylor has defended redistricting efforts in Tennessee as a “compliance measure” in response to the 2026 US Supreme Court ruling that he says prohibits the consideration of racial data when redrawing political boundaries. Asked about his top priorities in such a diverse district spanning downtown Memphis to rural Fayette County, Taylor pointed to inflation. “Everybody feels the pain right now,” he said. “When I filled up my car the other day, it was $112. People feel the pinch at the gas pump. They feel higher prices when they go to the grocery store. Everything we do costs more.” Civil Miller-Watkins, an eighth-grade math teacher in Fayette County who was drawn into District 9 and plans to vote for Pearson, said the needs of voters in her area differ from those in Memphis. Rural voters worry about access to broadband, ambulances, grocery stores and schools, she said. “All of these interests are very legitimate,” Miller-Watkins said. “But I don’t know if any community can say they’re going to have effective representation.” Pearson, the Democrat, says he’s campaigned in 15 counties that now come under the district and economic hardship is the common thread. “That’s hurting people who are working class in Memphis, just like it’s hurting farmers in Savannah, Tennessee,” he said. “We have a lot more in common.” Urban 96% Suburban 4% Shelby County 737,000 people live in an urban county in District 9 Tipton County 31,000 live in a suburban county District 9 After Urban 35% Suburban 27% Memphis Nashville Williamson 107k Shelby 269k people Rutherford 39k Maury 33k Memphis area Small towns 22% Bedford 50k Lincoln 35k McNairy 26k Giles 30k Hardeman 25k Marshall 34k Lawrence 44k Hardin 27k Wayne 16k Moore 7k Rural 16% Before redistricting Fayette 25k Two panels comparing the counties that make up Tennessee’s 9th Congressional District before and after the 2026 redraw, with each county drawn at an area proportional to its population. Before, the district is almost entirely one place: urban Shelby County, home to Memphis, fills the panel with roughly 737,000 people, beside a thin sliver for suburban Tipton County’s ~31,000. After, 767,872 people are spread across 15 counties in four groups. Urban counties make up 35% of the district; suburban counties comprise 27%, small towns 22% and rural counties 16%. Note: Counties are grouped by the National Center for Health Statistics urban–rural classification. “Large central metro” was renamed to “Urban”, “Large fringe metro” to “Suburban”, “Micropolitan” to “Small towns” and “Noncore” was renamed “Rural” in this graphic. Sources: US Census; NCHS Urban-Rural Classification Scheme; Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury (2026 district); All About Redistricting, Loyola Law School (2022 district) Pearson said he was concerned that some voters were confused about which district they were in and that this could hurt turnout. Pearson’s advocacy for criminal justice reform and affordability has appealed to younger Democratic Party voters like 27-year-old Marko Jankov. But Jankov, who identifies as a Democratic Socialist, lives in a part of Memphis that was moved out of the 9th District and he said he was less motivated to vote for other Democrats when polls showed them unlikely to win. “They want to make it a psychological thing, where you think you can’t win,” Jankov said. The changes are exposing a rural-urban divide. Debby Gould, president of the non-partisan League of Women Voters of Tennessee, said voters of all backgrounds had concerns. “This is a time when we really have to strengthen urban-rural links and to come up with shared values,” she said. “Because rural voters are also feeling left out on this.” Hickey, the Williamson County Republican chair, said it was up to candidates to show they could work for all their constituents: “They’re going to have to put a lot of miles in their car.” Opening photo Elzey Avenue in Memphis, a dividing line between Congressional District 9 and Congressional District 5, following a Republican-led effort to redistrict Memphis. REUTERS/Seth Herald Sources US Census Bureau (2020 Census redistricting data, TIGER/Line); Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury (2026 congressional districts); All About Redistricting, Loyola Law School (2022 congressional districts); State of Tennessee and the City of Memphis Engineering Division (city limits); Tennessee Department of Transportation (roads). Additional contributions by Travis Hartman, Ben Kellerman and Tiana McGee Edited by Claudia Parsons, Kat Stafford and Julia Wolfe More from Reuters Graphics

item.title: トランプ氏、対ロシア制裁法の適用を発動直前に免除
item.description:
Kanishka Singh Jasper Ward
[ワシントン １６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Kanishka Singh　Jasper Ward

[ワシントン １６日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は先月署名した法律に基づくロシア関連の主要な制裁と関税の適用を免除した。ロシア製品への関税や、同国の石油・天然ガスを購入する国への制裁が対象となる。これらは数日後に発効する予定だった。

ホワイトハウスが１６日に公表した大統領令で、トランプ氏は適用免除が米国の国益にかなうと説明した。免除はトランプ氏または政府高官が「追加措置が適切」と判断するまで有効となる。

同法は共和党の故リンゼー・グラム上院議員が推進し、トランプ氏が９月中旬に署名した。ロシア産原油・天然ガスの輸入上位５カ国から米国に輸入される製品に、３０日以内に最大１００％の関税を課す内容となっていた。法律成立から３０日後以降にロシア産と知りながら石油・天然ガスを購入した国や、ロシアの制裁逃れを支援する上位５カ国も対象に含まれていた。

トランプ氏は大統領令で「現時点でこうした適用免除を行うことが米国の国益にかなうとする証明書を議会に提出した」と述べた。同法では、大統領は制裁が国益にかなわないと判断したと議会に通知するだけで、制裁を免除できる。

バージニア州選出のドン・ベイヤー民主党下院議員は、今回の措置を強く批判した。声明で「トランプ氏は今回もプーチン（ロシア大統領）に屈し、パートナーであるウクライナを再び裏切った。ロシアの違法な侵略戦争を罰するための法律に込められた議会の明確な意思にも背いている」と述べた。

トランプ氏は最近ロシアと結んだ軽油に関する合意でも、一部の共和党議員を含む複数の米上院議員から批判を受けていた。

item.title: Pumas UNAM vence al Atlante en el torneo mexicano con doblete del brasileño Juninho
item.description: Pumas UNAM ganó el viernes 2-1 de visita al Atlante con un doblete del brasileño Juninho en la duodécima jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pumas UNAM ganó el viernes 2-1 de visita al Atlante con un doblete del brasileño Juninho en la duodécima jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano. Con su cuarta victoria en el torneo, el club de la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México llegó a 16 puntos y se ubicó en el noveno lugar de la tabla general, cerca de la zona que da acceso a la postemporada. Los primeros ocho lugares al término de las 17 jornadas de la fase regular obtienen ese boleto. En el partido disputado en el estadio Azteca de Ciudad de México, Pumas se puso en ventaja a los 42 minutos cuando Juninho remató de derecha en el área chica tras un pase de cabeza del paraguayo Robert Morales. Atlante empató en tiempo de reposición de la primera parte con un potente disparo de Luis Calzadilla desde fuera del área, que metió el balón pegado al poste izquierdo. Pumas selló el triunfo a los 72 minutos con el doblete de Juninho, quien cerró una jugada de contragolpe con un potente zurdazo en el área tras recibir un pase del panameño Adalberto Carrasquilla. En los otros partidos del viernes, Atlas ganó 2-0 de visita a Necaxa con goles del belga Ryan Mmaee y del argentino Manuel Capasso. Con su sexto triunfo, los "Rojinegros" del Atlas llegaron a 21 puntos y se ubicaron momentáneamente en el segundo lugar general, por debajo de América que registra las mismas unidades, pero una mejor diferencia de gol. Por su parte, Tijuana y Puebla empataron 0-0. La actividad continuará el sábado cuando Santos Laguna enfrente a Querétaro, Guadalajara juegue como local ante Tigres UANL, América visite a León, Toluca reciba al Atlético de San Luis y el vigente campeón Cruz Azul enfrente a Bravos de Ciudad Juárez. La jornada concluirá el domingo cuando Monterrey reciba a Pachuca.

item.dc:creator: Reuters

item.title: Figueroa loses WBA featherweight title after missing weight
item.description: American Brandon Figueroa has been stripped of his WBA featherweight title after hitting the scales 1.4 pounds over the 126-pound weight limit for Saturday's fight against Tomoki Kameda of Japan, organisers said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: American Brandon Figueroa has been stripped of his WBA featherweight title after hitting the scales 1.4 pounds over the 126-pound weight limit for Saturday's fight against Tomoki Kameda of Japan, organisers said on Friday. Kameda, 35, will be able to clinch the vacant title if he wins the fight, which will go ahead as scheduled in Las Vegas. "Honestly, it's disrespectful, because I'm here, I suffered too. I did my thing. I'm ready for tomorrow," Kameda said, speaking via a translator. "It has been 18 months since I fought, but look at me, look how shredded I am. You know I'm ready. Everything remains the same, I'm going for the title tomorrow." Figueroa, 29, clinched the featherweight title in February after beating Briton Nick Ball in Liverpool. If he wins the fight against Kameda, the title will remain vacant.

item.title: Delegates walked out of IMF steering committee meeting when Russian official spoke, sources say
item.description: Many delegates to the International Monetary Fund's steering committee walked out of a meeting on Saturday when Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov addressed the group in Russian, three sources familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, Jan Strupczewski
item.content:encoded: Many delegates to the International Monetary Fund's steering committee walked out of a meeting on Saturday when Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov addressed the group in Russian, three sources familiar with the matter said. Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 has roiled the International Monetary and Financial Committee, preventing it from reaching consensus statements in the years since. There were deep divisions again at this week's annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok, as new [USN:L8N4620FR TEXT:"tensions flared between the US and Ukraine"]. "Many delegations walked out, including members of the European Union," one of the sources told Reuters. A second official in the room said nearly a dozen delegates left the room when the Russian official began speaking. Delegates from Denmark, Sweden, Finland, Norway, Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia were among those who left, the official said. "The Ukraine war is existential for us in Europe," one European diplomat said. "We cannot normalize relations with Russia." Germany on Thursday [USN:SPN460013 TEXT:"warned against efforts to bring Russia back on to the international stage"] after Siluanov attended a meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bankers, just over a month after the US had hosted his first in-person G20 appearance since Russia invaded Ukraine, at a meeting in Asheville, North Carolina. US Treasury Undersecretary Erin Browne told Reuters the same day that Washington, the current leader of the G20 nations, supported Russia's presence despite European concerns. "We think it's really important if you're going to solve a crisis, you need to have open dialogue and open conversation," she told Reuters. "And you can't have ... dialogue, and you can't have resolution to conflict if no one's talking to one another." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, speaking at a European Union summit on Friday, blasted US President Donald Trump's [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"diesel deal"] with Russia and welcomed the prospect of European allies stepping up their role in peace talks. EU leaders rallied around Zelenskiy after Trump again criticised Ukraine, calling its strikes on Russian refineries a "disgrace". The EU was hosting Zelenskiy at one of the most difficult moments for Ukraine, with missiles and drones raining down on Ukrainian cities and fears that the US could pull back intelligence sharing and weapons support from Kyiv.

item.title: German minister seeks debt-brake exemption to sustain Ukraine aid
item.description: Germany's development minister is seeking an exemption from the country's debt brake, a constitutional limit on government borrowing, for Ukraine funding, arguing that much of Germany's civilian support for Ukraine comes from her ministry's budget.
item.dc:creator: Maria Martinez
item.content:encoded: Germany's development minister is seeking an exemption from the country's debt brake, a constitutional limit on government borrowing, for Ukraine funding, arguing that much of Germany's civilian support for Ukraine comes from her ministry's budget. "The Russian attacks are more severe than ever, leading to more deaths, more destruction, more suffering. But as budget cuts for development assistance continue, we simply will not be able to maintain our support for Ukraine at this level," Reem Alabali Radovan told Reuters on Friday, on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank meetings. Funding for Ukraine in her ministry's budget amounts to about €330 million ($371 million) this year, down from €670 million in 2022 and €750 million in 2023. "At this point, it is not a political decision; we just face massive cuts and it will no longer be possible," Alabali Radovan said. "This is especially hard as the money is wisely invested in Ukraine's and Europe's stability." Alabali Radovan is a member of the Social Democrats, the junior partner of the governing coalition led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz's CDU. Her proposal has the backing of Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, a member of the conservative CDU, but faces opposition from other members of the party who oppose further exceptions to borrowing rules beyond those already approved, such as for defence spending. "I am already prioritising support for Ukraine, but there are many other crises and conflicts, too. And we work in the long term, which means large parts of our budget are already committed," Alabali Radovan said. "That means the cuts hit crisis instruments above all, because – naturally – they work with flexible funds that are not yet pre-committed." Alabali Radovan added that she supports Merz's call for other countries to contribute more. "We are the strongest supporters, and I believe others can and should contribute more," she said. ($1 = 0.8887 euros)

item.title: Students, trade unions and Yellow Vests set to protest across France
item.description: Tens of thousands of people are expected to protest across France on Saturday, as students, trade unionists and remnants of the Yellow Vest movement join forces to demonstrate against high prices and the country's fraying social model.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Pineau
item.content:encoded: Tens of thousands of people are expected to protest across France on Saturday, as students, trade unionists and remnants of the Yellow Vest movement join forces to demonstrate against high prices and the country's fraying social model. The initial wave of protests began last month at high schools in Paris' poor northern suburbs, where anger over teacher absences and shabby facilities quickly morphed into a nationwide movement against inequality, weak public spending and falling standards. The protests come at a difficult time for France, as President Emmanuel Macron enters [USN:L1N45Y033 TEXT:"the final stretch of his presidency"], leaving behind a polarised electorate and a fragmented domestic political situation. Investors ditching French debt, driving borrowing costs [USN:L8N45R0RA TEXT:"to their highest levels in more than two decades"], have also underlined the country's long struggle to get its [USN:L8N45A0ZG TEXT:"public finances"] in order. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Thursday that authorities [USN:L6N4610XN TEXT:"fear unrest during the protests"]. The government blames the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) for inflaming the protests, an accusation LFI denies. "This is a moment of fatigue in the country," Lecornu said. "We are in an atmosphere of perma-crisis: wars, inflation, and issues surrounding purchasing power." Opposition chief Jordan Bardella, whose far-right National Rally leads in the polls ahead of next year's presidential election, said he expected violence. "I'm extremely concerned," he said during a visit to the Paris car show. "It will be a day of chaos for France." VIOLENT PROTESTS Lecornu has said the protests have been among the most violent in decades, with more than 900 police injured since the start of the protests. The police have also drawn criticism for their response [USN:L6N45V0HM TEXT:"due to a grisly list of injuries"], including one adolescent who had his hand blown off after picking up a stun grenade. The internal police watchdog is investigating at least two dozen cases of alleged police violence. France suspended the use of stun grenades for the student demonstrations, but Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said they could be used in Saturday's protest. "If there were to be clashes, all types of intermediate weapons can be used," he told Telematin on Friday. Calls on social media for members of past protest movements to join the fray appear to have worked, raising questions about just how large the protests could grow. The Yellow Vest movement started in 2018 as a protest against taxes on diesel before morphing into an outpouring of anger at high living costs and income inequality. However, things have been largely quiet since Macron agreed to billions of euros in tax cuts. Yannick Maillou, a teacher from La Crèche in western France, joined the Yellow Vests in 2018 and remains involved in the movement. He said there were several nearby meeting points for protesters to gather on Saturday, with unions also calling on their members to join. "Groups of people providing medical assistance are forming in anticipation of police violence," he said. Myrtil Devillers, another Yellow Vest protester, said he was sympathetic to the protesters' "explosive catch-all of grievances" although he won't be protesting on Saturday as he is abroad. "I was a Yellow Vest protester when petrol cost €1.40 a litre, so imagine how I feel now that it's €2.20," he said. "The justice system is complaining; the education system is complaining; the healthcare sector is complaining; my friends who run businesses are complaining."

item.title: Could Trump interfere in the midterms? | On Assignment
item.description: Reporters lay out scenarios where Trump could try to sway election results.
item.content:encoded:
Follow on Apple or Spotify . Listen on the Reuters app.

As President Donald Trump seeks greater influence over how elections are run, election officials across the country are bracing for disputes over voting, ballot counting and the certification of results. Reuters reporters Peter Eisler and Mike Spector join On Assignment to discuss the scenarios officials and legal experts fear could test the boundaries of federal authority before and after the 2026 midterms. Further Reading Nine ways the Trump administration could interfere with the midterms Trump claims voting by noncitizens is rampant in America. The numbers tell another story . How Trump is moving to control U.S. elections, one state at a time

item.title: Analistas pierden la confianza en Adobe y crece el temor de que la IA erosione su negocio
item.description: Las rebajas de Wells Fargo y HSBC reflejan el temor a que las herramientas de inteligencia artificial reduzcan la demanda de Photoshop y presionen los márgenes de Adobe.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Vlastelica
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — La opinión de los analistas sobre Adobe Inc. ( ADBE ) nunca había sido tan negativa, en un contexto cada vez más marcado por la convicción de que al fabricante de software para profesionales creativos le resultará difícil competir en la era de la inteligencia artificial. Esta semana, dos analistas rebajaron la calificación de la acción, uniéndose así a un coro cada vez mayor de escépticos que temen que las ofertas de las compañías de IA disminuyan la demanda de productos como Photoshop, lo que disminuiría el potencial de crecimiento a largo plazo de Adobe. La primera rebaja de calificación esta semana vino de la mano de Wells Fargo Securities, que este lunes rebajó la acción dos niveles, pasando de “sobreponderar” a “infraponderar” y disminuyendo su precio objetivo a 12 meses de US$270 a US$225. Esto elevó a siete el número de calificaciones equivalentes a “vender”, la cifra más alta registrada hasta la fecha, en comparación con las cero que había a mediados de 2025. Ver más: De Microsoft a Adobe: Trump suspende a ocho tecnológicas de un programa para obtener la Green Card “Empiezan a aparecer ahora señales más significativas de debilidad en el perfil de crecimiento de Adobe”, escribió el analista Michael Turrin, refiriéndose a los resultados del tercer trimestre de la empresa del mes pasado, que calificó de “bastante moderados”. Agregó que la capacidad de Adobe para cumplir sus objetivos anuales parece “difícil, dados los últimos comentarios de la dirección sobre el aplazamiento de cualquier subida de precios en sus productos creativos principales”. Este martes, el analista de HSBC, Stephen Bersey, rebajó la calificación de las acciones de “comprar” a “mantener” y redujo su precio objetivo de US$310 a US$267, señalando que Adobe es “un candidato realista para la disrupción impulsada por la IA”. Los analistas han rebajado la calificación de las acciones de Adobe al menos 15 veces en el 2026, incluyendo las rebajas de esta semana. Como resultado, el consenso de recomendaciones de Adobe, un indicador de la proporción de calificaciones de compra, mantenimiento y venta ha caído a 3,16 sobre cinco, un mínimo histórico. La calificación promedio de consenso para las empresas del índice de software S&P 500 es de 4,65, lo que indica un optimismo mucho mayor. Ver más: Adobe prevé que compras online asistidas por IA aumenten 130% en temporada navideña La preocupaciones sobre el impacto disruptivo de la IA han sido un tema central para los inversionistas en software este año. El sector sufrió una fuerte caída a inicios de 2026, cuando el lanzamiento continuo de productos por parte de empresas nativas de IA, como OpenAI y Anthropic, generó ventas generalizadas. Aunque la confianza en el sector se ha recuperado en gran parte, ya que los inversionistas consideran que algunos tipos de software son difíciles de sustituir, Adobe continúa siendo una excepción notable. Las acciones han descendido casi un 30% este año, en comparación con una ganancia del 3,7% del ETF iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector, un indicador ampliamente usado del sector. Adobe se encamina a su tercer año consecutivo con una caída superior al 20%, una prolongada venta masiva que refleja cómo se percibe a la empresa como un ejemplo paradigmático de la disrupción causada por la IA. Ver más: Oracle vs. Adobe: por qué Wall Street evalúa de forma distinta sus apuestas por la IA A los inversionistas les preocupa que los usuarios cancelen sus suscripciones a Photoshop para usar herramientas de compañías como OpenAI o Anthropic para generar imágenes a partir de indicaciones. Si bien Adobe ofrece sus propias funciones de inteligencia artificial, existe el temor de que la competencia en este campo presione su poder de fijación de precios y afecte sus márgenes de beneficio. Esta preocupación fue la razón principal de la rebaja de calificación de HSBC. Bersey ve competencia en los “clones de Adobe con programación intuitiva”, refiriéndose al software desarrollado mediante IA. Entre las ofertas gratuitas con programación intuitiva de una compañía llamada ArtCraft se incluyen “versiones de Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, Acrobat, After Effects e InDesign”, escribió, citando informes de prensa. Dicha competencia “crea riesgos importantes para Adobe”, escribió, aunque además reconoce que estos servicios suponen riesgos para los usuarios. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Mongolia becomes new donor to World Bank's fund for poorest countries
item.description: The World Bank Group said on Saturday that Mongolia has become a new donor to the International Development Association fund for the poorest countries, after previously spending nearly three decades as a recipient of IDA funding.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The World Bank Group said on Saturday that Mongolia has become a new donor to the International Development Association fund for the poorest countries, after previously spending nearly three decades as a recipient of IDA funding. The development lender said that Mongolia's parliament approved a 4.8 billion tugrik ($1.3 million) contribution to the latest IDA funding round, marking a milestone in the country's development journey. Since becoming a World Bank member country in 1991, Mongolia has received more than $1.62 billion in development financing, including IDA support for transport, rural development, health and education. Mongolia graduated from IDA support in July 2020, becoming a client of the World Bank's main lending arm for middle-income countries, the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development. "Mongolia’s contribution to IDA21 marks an important milestone in our longstanding partnership with the World Bank and reflects our commitment to international solidarity," Mongolian Finance Minister Mendsaikhan Zagdjav said in a statement released by the World Bank. "Having benefited firsthand from IDA’s support, we recognize the vital role of concessional financing in helping countries reduce poverty, build resilience, and expand opportunities. As we continue to advance Mongolia's own development priorities, we are proud to support other countries in pursuing theirs."

item.title: Bruins escape 2-goal hole, emerge with win over Ducks
item.description: Elias Lindholm scored to break a third-period tie, capping a two-point performance as the visiting Boston Bruins registered a come-from-behind 4-2 victory over the Anaheim Ducks on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Elias Lindholm scored to break a third-period tie, capping a two-point performance as the visiting Boston Bruins registered a come-from-behind 4-2 victory over the Anaheim Ducks on Friday. David Pastrnak netted one goal and one assist for the Bruins, who scored four unanswered goals, three on the power play, to run their winning streak to four games. Frederic Brunet potted his first career NHL goal, Matthew Poitras added a tally, and Pavel Zacha and James Hagens each logged two assists. Bruins goaltender Michael DiPietro made 25 saves to earn his first NHL victory in his sixth game and fourth start. Tim Washe and Beckett Sennecke scored for the Ducks, who squandered a 2-0 lead and have dropped their second game in a row. Goalie Lukas Dostal stopped 18 shots. While the Bruins converted three of their four power-play opportunities, the Ducks were blanked on five chances with the extra skater. Anaheim also mustered only four shots on goal in the third period. After watching his team erase a 2-0 deficit, Lindholm put Boston on top at 8:18 of the third period with a tap-in tally set up by Zacha while on a power play. Poitras added an insurance goal eight minutes later when he finished a 2-on-1 rush on a setup from Hagens. Anaheim tallied twice late in the first period. Washe opened the scoring with 37.3 seconds remaining in the frame, finding the twine with his long shot from the point that made it through a screen and DiPietro's legs. Sennecke doubled the lead 21 seconds later, notching his fifth of the season by finishing a three-way passing play. Brunet, a 2022 fifth-round draft choice, halved Boston's deficit at 3:15 of the second period. He sent a long shot from the blue line that made it through the maze of traffic for his milestone marker. Pastrnak tied the clash with another man-advantage goal at 3:26 of the third period, pouncing on a loose puck during a scramble for his third of the campaign. Pastrnak took sole possession of the fourth spot on the Bruins' all-time goals list with his 423rd career tally, passing Brad Marchand. He trails only Johnny Bucyk (545 goals), Phil Esposito (459) and Patrice Bergeron (427). --Field Level Media

item.title: BOJ may need to tighten faster if inflation beats forecast, IMF says
item.description: The Bank of Japan is "doing the right thing" by normalising monetary policy and may need to raise interest rates faster if inflation rises more than expected, a senior International Monetary Fund official told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Japan is "doing the right thing" by normalising monetary policy and may need to raise interest rates faster if inflation rises more than expected, a senior International Monetary Fund official told Reuters. Japan must also clarify how it plans to fund its big spending plans and lay out a medium-term fiscal framework to ease market concerns about fiscal risks, said Krishna Srinivasan, director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department. "I would say that they are doing the right thing at this point," Srinivasan said on the BOJ's efforts to lift its policy rate towards levels deemed neutral to the economy. "If inflation rises faster than expected, you have to start tightening faster because you don't want inflation expectations to get un-anchored. It's data dependent," he said in an interview on Friday. The remarks came ahead of the BOJ's key policy meeting later this month, when it [USN:L4N45S011 TEXT:"could keep rates steady"] but drop hawkish hints that would reinforce dominant market expectations of a December hike. Inflationary pressures from the Middle East conflict and brisk AI-demand were among key themes discussed by policymakers gathering for this week's annual IMF meetings in Bangkok. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda, who attended the IMF meetings, said on [USN:L1N4620G5 TEXT:"Friday"] the central bank will focus on anchoring underlying inflation around its 2% target and won't tolerate any overshoot, stressing anew its resolve to continue raising interest rates. For Japan, a weak yen adds to factors pushing up inflation by boosting the cost of raw material imports. Such mounting price pressures prodded the BOJ to raise rates to a 31-year high of 1.25% in [USN:L1N459138 TEXT:"September"], following a hike in June. Many analysts expect another rate increase by year-end. Japan also conducted a rare, coordinated intervention with the US on [USN:L1N43Z05E TEXT:"July 31"] to prevent the currency's slide to near 40-year lows from destabilising financial markets. In staff analysis included in its report on Asia's economy, the IMF said a big portion of yen moves since mid-2025 had little to do with fundamental factors such as yield differentials, and instead co-moved with speculative positions in yen futures. "Japan has a deep foreign exchange market, so as a first line of defense, they have allowed the exchange rate to move," Srinivasan said. "Bottom line, I would say that the Japanese authorities are fully committed to a freely floating exchange rate. I've had many discussions with them. So I don't doubt that at all," he said when asked if the recent yen intervention was justified. FISCAL FRAMEWORK NEEDED Rising global bond yields have also drawn attention at this week's IMF meetings as debt in advanced economies, including Japan, expanded after years of heavy spending. Markets worry that Japan may add to its already huge debt pile with the administration's big spending plans and a two-year cut to the consumption tax from April next year. Srinivasan said Japan has in fact seen fiscal consolidation proceed more than any other G7 country since the pandemic due in part to rising tax revenues. "Markets are concerned about the fiscal risks because of the uncertainty" on how Japan would pay for the fresh spending and tax-cut plans, he said. "Japan also would benefit from having a medium-term fiscal framework."

item.title: Major development banks step up support for critical minerals value chains
item.description: Multilateral development banks (MDBs) will strengthen efforts to help mineral-rich developing economies add more value to their resources by moving beyond extraction into processing, refining and manufacturing, according to an outline of a critical minerals collaboration framework published on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Multilateral development banks (MDBs) will strengthen efforts to help mineral-rich developing economies add more value to their resources by moving beyond extraction into processing, refining and manufacturing, according to an outline of a critical minerals collaboration framework published on Saturday. The banks involved include the World Bank, the African Development Bank, the Asian Development Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the European Investment Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank, according to the outline The October framework calls for coordinated support across critical mineral supply chains, including financing, infrastructure and policy aimed at creating jobs, boosting domestic value addition, attracting private investment and supporting low-carbon transition MDBs plan to support mineral corridors incorporating power, transport, logistics, water and digital infrastructure, while strengthening project preparation and using co-financing, guarantees and other financing tools to mobilise capital and accelerate private sector investments They will also seek closer alignment on environmental and social standards, coordinate support to governments and better connect mining projects with infrastructure and industrial development An MDB working group will coordinate implementation of the framework's objectives and report annually to the Heads of MDBs Group on progress

item.title: Dollar heads for weekly loss as Fed hike bets fade, AI jitters linger
item.description: This week, the dollar faced a notable drop due to decreased expectations for interest rate increases from the Federal Reserve. Federal officials' remarks have led to steadying Treasury yields, which in turn weakened the dollar's position. Concurrently, the euro and yen gained ground, with the euro nearing a weekly rise. Investors are increasingly wary of fiscal risks, especially as shifts in economic conditions unfold.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The dollar was lower on Friday and on track for its first weekly fall in more than a month against the euro and the yen, reflecting fading expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike and lingering concerns about an AI-driven equity selloff.Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer price readings initially rattled markets this week, but comments from Fed officials signaling no urgency to tighten policy further helped stabilize Treasury yields and eroded support for the dollar.AI stocks fell sharply this week and the stress spread to parts of the credit market as investors who have crowded into bets all along the supply chain worry data centre operators might not manage to be profitable in time to pay their debts. What I found most interesting today and more broadly this week, is how closely the dollar has been tied to the AI trade, said Matt Weller, global head of market research at StoneX in Michigan. Usually if we see a sell off in tech stocks you would expect the greenback to get a safe-haven bid. We are seeing an element of that into bonds, but the dollar is actually falling. The dollar index, which measures it against six major peers, fell 0.17% to 101.87 and was set for a 0.35% weekly drop.The pound and the Swiss franc led gains against the dollar this week, with the latter buoyed by safe-haven demand and expectations that even in a lower-rates environment Switzerland is unlikely to cut policy rates below the current zero level.Sterling rose 0.31% to $1.3314 and was up 0.63% on the week, while the dollar fell 0.25% against the Swiss franc to 0.8246, leaving it down 0.67% for the week. The franc has gained more than 1.4% in the last two sessions.Markets assign an 83% probability to the Fed keeping rates unchanged later this month, up from 49% a month earlier, the CME FedWatch Tool shows.At the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh offered no clues about future rate decisions, saying he does not prejudge meetings. I don't think there is enough support in (the) committee, particularly from the governors, for a rate hike in October. It still leaves December an unanswered question and there is a lot to happen between now and then, said John Velis, Americas macro strategist at BNY in New York.Euro Area Fiscal Risks Still In FocusFiscal risks in France remained in the background after the jump in the French debt risk premium in early October.The euro was last up 0.08% to $1.1227 after climbing 0.56% on Thursday in its biggest daily rise in two months, putting it on track for a 0.23% weekly gain.Investors expect US President Donald Trump to steer clear of any escalation in the Middle East or Ukraine, as a broader conflict could hurt his standing ahead of midterm elections by fuelling inflation.Against the yen the dollar slipped 0.08% to 158.11, leaving the Japanese currency on track for a 0.13% weekly rise after dropping for four consecutive weeks as the Iran conflict supported the greenback.Higher oil prices recently have been boosting the dollar while weighing on the currencies of energy-importing countries, such as those tied to the euro and yen.BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda on Friday reiterated the risks of underlying inflation overshooting the central bank's 2% target.

item.title: Canada women snap world champion England's 41-match unbeaten run
item.description: Canada’s women snapped world champion England’s 41-match unbeaten run with a 24-21 victory in Toronto on Friday, achieving a goal they have long been working toward.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Fernandes
item.content:encoded: Canada’s women snapped world champion England’s 41-match unbeaten run with a 24-21 victory in Toronto on Friday, achieving a goal they have long been working toward. One month after halting England's 39-match winning streak following a 26-26 draw in Exeter, a late try from Shoshanah Seumanutafa put Canada ahead with less than three minutes left to play. “Definitely special," Canada captain Sophie de Goede told reporters after the landmark win. "I think there were a lot of ups and downs throughout that game and we really had to grind it out and find a way, and that's kind of the DNA of our team and our group. "So, I think more than anything, I feel proud of the way that we found a way to win that game, and it wasn't easy.” The opener of a two-game Rugby Rematch Tour between the growing rivals drew an electric crowd to BMO Field as Canada returned to home soil for the first time since finishing runner-up to the Red Roses at last year's World Cup. "I think it's a little bit more than just the score at the end because we won on so many levels today," Canada's Justine Pelletier said. "Off the field, just the crowd, being home, and there's so much going on around. And I think that win at the end on the pitch was just the cherry on (top)." Savannah Bauder, Alysha Corrigan and DaLeaka Menin also scored tries for Canada, while Maddie Feaunati, Zoe Harrison and Sarah Bern added one each for England. England's unbeaten run had stretched back to their World Cup final defeat by New Zealand in 2022. Canada’s last win over the Red Roses came in 2016 at the Women's Rugby Super Series. “It was good to beat England, but I think for a few years now we knew that we could beat them," Pelletier said. "It was just a matter of time and a matter of putting every detail together." For top-ranked England, having a target on their back is nothing new. “The bit we always remember is we're at the top, and when you're at the top, people want to bring you down as quick as they can,” England captain Megan Jones said, adding that the team take "huge pride" in their unbeaten run. Jones also praised the atmosphere in Toronto, where 18,621 fans rocked the stands all night in chilly conditions, setting an attendance record for a women’s rugby match in North America. "We're the biggest advocates for the game," Jones said of players. "So we're always going to try and grow the game as much as we can, and Canada definitely did that in tenfold today." Canada and England will face off in the second game of the Rugby Rematch Tour on October 23 in Ottawa.

item.title: Nathan MacKinnon’s 4-point night powers Avalanche past Penguins
item.description: Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists to lead the Colorado Avalanche to a 5-2 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday in Denver.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists to lead the Colorado Avalanche to a 5-2 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday in Denver. Artturi Lehkonen scored twice while Gabriel Landeskog and T.J. Hughes added goals for the Avalanche, who went 2-0-1 while playing three games in four nights. Martin Necas had three assists, Cale Makar added two, and Mackenzie Blackwood made 29 saves. Evgeni Malkin and Bryan Rust got the goals for the Penguins, who are 1-4-1 in their past six. Arturs Silovs turned away 27 shots. Colorado scored the only three goals of the second period to go up 4-2. Lehkonen notched his second goal of the night 25 seconds into the frame, tying it 2-2. He knocked down the rebound of MacKinnon's shot off the goalpost with his glove and scored from the crease. Landeskog gave Colorado the lead for good at 4:24, slamming a Brock Nelson pass into the open side of the net. Hughes scored his first career NHL goal when he tipped in MacKinnon's pass with 5:03 left in the period, four seconds after an Avalanche power play expired. MacKinnon added a power-play goal on a one-timer from just above the left dot with 4:54 left in the third to make it five straight goals for the Avalanche. He has 16 points (six goals and 10 assists) in eight games this season. Silovs stopped MacKinnon's penalty-shot attempt 15 seconds before Landeskog's goal. Pittsburgh jumped ahead 2-0 with two goals 29 seconds apart in the first period. Malkin scored as he cut across the slot after charging down the right wing. He shot as he fell and beat Blackwood 8:28 into the game. Rust then tipped in Sidney Crosby's pass on a 2-on-1 rush at 8:57. Colorado got on the board at 11:01 of the first when Lehkonen tipped in a pass from MacKinnon off the rush. New Avalanche assistant coach Brett McLean made his debut behind the bench after replacing Dave Hakstol, who departed to become the head coach at Arizona State. --Field Level Media

item.title: Apple appoints Meta veteran Scott Tucker to lead global litigation
item.description: Tucker will oversee commercial and patent litigation worldwide and legal matters involving Apple's financial services as the company faces mounting lawsuits under General Counsel Jennifer Newstead ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Mark Gurman Apple Inc. has tapped a longtime Meta Platforms Inc. executive as its new litigation chief, bolstering its legal team at a time when the iPhone maker faces a growing array of lawsuits. The company has hired Scott Tucker, a longtime deputy general counsel and litigation chief at Meta, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The move reunites Tucker with new Apple General Counsel Jennifer Newstead, who is bringing on a trusted lieutenant from her time at the social networking giant. Tucker is becoming Apple’s vice president of global litigation and financial services, a newly created position overseeing commercial and patent litigation worldwide, said the people, who asked not to be named because the move isn’t public. He’ll also manage legal matters involving the company’s financial offerings.  The appointment means Heather Grenier, Apple’s current vice president of commercial and competition litigation, will move one level lower in the organisation, reporting to Tucker instead of directly to Newstead. Grenier will still remain on Newstead’s legal leadership team.  Tucker, in addition to his tenure at Meta, previously held a senior legal position at Morgan Stanley, giving him experience relevant to his new financial services responsibilities. Newstead took over as Apple’s general counsel in March after serving as Meta’s top lawyer for six years. Kyle Andeer, another senior member of Apple’s legal department and its longtime vice president managing regulatory and product-related legal matters, is seeing his role expand. He is gaining oversight of international legal matters and functions involving online child safety, cybersecurity and law enforcement. Spokespeople for Apple and Meta declined to comment.  The changes are part of a broader reorganisation under Newstead, who oversees legal and government affairs. Apple recently hired Nate Gatten, a former American Airlines Group Inc. executive, as its vice president of government affairs. The company has also appointed new government affairs leads for different international regions. Apple combined its legal and government affairs groups under Newstead following the recent retirements of Lisa Jackson, the former head of environmental, policy and social initiatives, and previous top lawyer Kate Adams. Former Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook, now the company’s executive chairman, has also taken a leading role in government affairs. Apple is waging a variety of legal battles, including a sweeping US antitrust lawsuit, its long-running dispute with Epic Games Inc. over App Store restrictions, and litigation related to privacy and delays to Siri features. The company has faced billions of dollars in judgments and settlements in recent years, while regulators in the US and Europe have challenged business practices central to the iPhone maker’s operations. Some Apple executives believe the company hasn’t fared as well in court as it should have, particularly in litigation involving the App Store. Those setbacks have forced Apple to change its commission structure and the circumstances under which it can charge developers. The changes threaten to significantly slow growth in Apple’s services business, a key driver of revenue expansion in recent years. A slowdown in that business would deal a major blow to the company’s overall financial performance. Even in the best of times, overseeing Apple’s litigation is a difficult job. The Cupertino, California-based company is among the most frequently sued businesses in the world, facing cases ranging from slip-and-fall claims at its retail stores to multibillion-dollar antitrust disputes. Grenier took over the role under particularly challenging circumstances, replacing her predecessor just before Apple’s landmark trial against Epic Games began in 2021. Her tenure has also spanned two major leadership transitions: the appointment of John Ternus as CEO and Newstead’s arrival. In recent weeks, Ternus has overseen a sweeping series of executive changes, including the appointment of new leaders for the App Store, events and corporate functions such as information security and real estate. The reshuffling also includes the departure of the longtime Apple Pay chief, the replacement of the company’s mergers and acquisitions head, and a reorganisation of the company’s hardware engineering division.

item.title: Carapaz joins NSN on three-year deal
item.description: Former Giro d'Italia winner and Olympic champion Richard Carapaz joined NSN Cycling Team on Friday, after leaving EF Education-EasyPost a year before the end of his contract.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former Giro d'Italia winner and Olympic champion Richard Carapaz joined NSN Cycling Team on Friday, after leaving EF Education-EasyPost a year before the end of his contract. The 33-year-old Ecuadorean, who won the Giro in 2019 and road race gold at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, signed a three-year deal with NSN, formerly known as Israel–Premier Tech. "I'm really looking forward to it, and to be honest, this reminds me a lot of when I signed my first professional contract, when I was incredibly excited about being in the WorldTour," Carapaz said in a statement. "The team has big ambitions to keep growing and already in my conversations with the performance team, it was clear we share the same desire to keep improving and achieve big things together." Carapaz, renowned for his climbing ability, won two stages at this year's Tour de France to finish eighth overall.

item.title: OpenAI poaches another SpaceX sales lead for cybersecurity business
item.description: Graham Seamans, who led xAI's sales team since August 2025, joins OpenAI's cyber team as the ChatGPT maker expands enterprise sales and explores new revenue streams ahead of a potential public listing ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Carmen Arroyo OpenAI has hired SpaceX’s Graham Seamans to lead sales for the firm’s cybersecurity business, the latest in a string of hires from Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence venture. Seamans, who had led xAI’s sales team since August 2025 and was part of the firm’s renewed push to sell the Grok chatbot to Wall Street, said he’s joining the developer behind ChatGPT to work on the cyber team. Seamans is the latest sales executive who OpenAI has hired from SpaceX’s AI units. Before joining xAI last year, Seamans had worked at MongoDB Inc. for about eight years, according to his LinkedIn. Since September, OpenAI has also hired Brian McCarthy and Ismail Elmas in Europe, both of whom had worked for coding automation startup Cursor, which was acquired by SpaceX for $60 billion in August. OpenAI has also hired other staffers from SpaceX’s AI compute team, including Uday Ruddarraju and Brent Mayo.  OpenAI is trying to expand its commercial reach by boosting sales from enterprise customers and creating new revenue sources such as advertising ahead of a potential public listing. Musk lost a lawsuit against OpenAI, which he helped form, arguing that the AI lab betrayed its mission to the public by changing to a for-profit business. He started a competing AI developer, xAI, which he then merged with SpaceX. OpenAI declined to comment.

item.title: Australia confirms first H5N1 bird flu case on sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island
item.description: Australia on Saturday confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu on the sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island, with the deadly virus found in the remote territory's vulnerable elephant seal population.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia on Saturday confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu on the sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island, with the deadly virus found in the remote territory's vulnerable elephant seal population. Australia's Chief Veterinary Officer Beth Cookson said official testing confirmed the highly pathogenic virus strain "in samples collected from an elephant seal and a kelp gull on Macquarie Island, marking the first H5 event on this island". Australia in June became the last continent to report bird flu, although the virus was detected in late 2025 on another of its sub-Antarctic territories, Heard Island, where more than 13,000 baby seals were killed by the virus, according to local media. Like Heard Island, Macquarie Island, a UNESCO World Heritage-listed territory located in the Southern Ocean halfway between Australia's Tasmania state and Antarctica, is a key breeding ground for southern elephant seals. The mammals, which can weigh up to 3,600 kg (7,936 pounds), are particularly susceptible to H5 bird flu, with pup mortality rates in some cases of more than 90%, according to the federal government. In August, Australia's environment department said it would withdraw personnel from a research station on Macquarie Island due to the "psycho-social risk to expeditioners of a potential H5 avian influenza outbreak". Expert assessments predicted the virus would likely cause a significant elephant seal mortality event during the upcoming breeding season, the environment department said.

item.title: サッカー＝インテル、主将マルティネスが負傷で7試合欠場へ─報道
item.description: ［１６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１６日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイタリア・セリエＡ、インテルの主将ラウタロ・マルティネスがハムストリングの負傷により今後７試合を欠場する見通しとなった。米スポーツ専門局ＥＳＰＮが１６日に伝えた。

マルティネスは１３日にホームで行われた欧州チャンピオンズリーグ（ＣＬ）、３─４で敗れたクラブ・ブルージュ（ベルギー）戦にフル出場し、２得点を記録。しかし、１５日に行った検査の結果、左ハムストリングの肉離れが判明した。

インテルのクリスティアン・キブ監督は１６日、「彼はしばらく離脱することになる。私は医師ではないが、復帰までの目安は聞いている。おそらく代表戦期間明けには戻ってくるだろう」と述べた。

これにより、マルティネスは１７日のボローニャ戦と、２１日のＣＬシャフタル・ドネツク（ウクライナ）戦の欠場が確実となった。１１月の代表戦期間までには、３１日に行われるＡＣミランとのダービーを含め、７試合が予定されている。

マルティネスは今季、公式戦７試合に出場して６得点を記録。昨季はセリエＡで１７ゴールを挙げ、自身２回目となるリーグ得点王に輝いている。

item.title: La caída de las acciones de CoreWeave refleja la división entre el miedo y la codicia ante la IA
item.description: El alza de los rendimientos de los bonos y la dependencia del crédito para financiar centros de datos presionan a CoreWeave, pese al respaldo de Jensen Huang y a la recomendación de compra de Deutsche ...
item.dc:creator: Jeran Wittenstein, Ryan Vlastelica
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — CoreWeave Inc. ( CRWV ) se ha visto envuelta en un tira y afloja entre los inversionistas que consideran que el aumento de los rendimientos de los bonos podría frenar el repunte del sector de la inteligencia artificial y aquellos que creen que la demanda de potencia de cálculo hará que esas preocupaciones queden obsoletas en poco tiempo. Las acciones del proveedor de servicios de computación en la nube se hundieron un 20% en las tres primeras sesiones de esta semana, incluyendo una caída superior al 15% este miércoles, mientras que el coste de su deuda se desplomaba hasta niveles que suelen indicar dificultades financieras. Este jueves por la mañana, el coste de proteger los bonos de CoreWeave frente al impago alcanzó el nivel intradía más alto jamás registrado, mientras que los swaps descontaban una probabilidad superior al 60% de que se produjera un impago en los próximos 5 años. Ver más: Fundadores de CoreWeave protegen sus fortunas con ventas de acciones por US$3.300 millones Sin embargo, el jueves por la tarde, la sensación de pánico parecía estar remitiendo, ya que las acciones repuntaron y pasaron a terreno positivo después de que Jensen Huang, CEO de Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ), accionista y proveedor de CoreWeave, expresara su confianza en la empresa. Además, Deutsche Bank calificó la ola de ventas como una “oportunidad de compra”. Las acciones cerraron la jornada con una subida del 5,9%, su mejor resultado en más de un mes. Pero el temor regresó el viernes, provocando una caída del 12% en las acciones de CoreWeave, lo que resultó en la peor semana para la acción desde noviembre, con un descenso del 25%. “El contexto macroeconómico ha creado un mercado en el que primero se vende y luego se hacen preguntas”, explicó Thomas DiFazio, estratega de fondos cotizados en bolsa de Roundhill Financial. “A corto plazo, es difícil afirmar con total seriedad que ya haya pasado el peligro”. Como proveedor de lo que se conoce como “ neocloud ”, CoreWeave se encuentra en el centro de la expansión de la infraestructura necesaria para desarrollar tecnología de IA. La seguridad de su deuda es una cuestión clave para los inversionistas, ya que su gasto en la construcción de centros de datos se financia mediante la emisión de bonos. Con el aumento de los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro y una inflación que se mantiene obstinadamente elevada, el coste de dicha financiación está elevándose rápidamente. Todo esto ha provocado una trayectoria accidentada para las acciones de CoreWeave. La acción ha subido más del 50% desde su problemática salida a bolsa en marzo de 2025, que tuvo que ser respaldada por Nvidia. No obstante, ha descendido un 12% este año y un 66% desde que alcanzara su máximo en junio de 2025, y se encuentra a menos de US$30 de su precio de salida. Ver más: CEO de Nvidia minimiza temores por la deuda de CoreWeave y sus acciones revierten pérdidas Sin embargo, el potencial alcista de CoreWeave es bastante evidente, ya que la demanda de servicios informáticos de inteligencia artificial sigue superando a la oferta. Y existen pocos indicios de que esa dinámica vaya a cambiar a corto plazo, señaló DiFazio. Esa fue la opinión del analista de Deutsche Bank, Brad Zelnick, quien mantiene una recomendación de “comprar” sobre la acción y anima a los inversionistas a hacerse con las acciones antes de que se recuperen por completo. CoreWeave cuenta con “una sólida base de clientes, un historial contrastado de ejecución, la conversión de la cartera de pedidos y un rendimiento de infraestructura líder”, escribió Zelnick en una nota de análisis este jueves. “Aunque se necesitará más capital, esto puede llevarse a cabo a un ritmo constante y cuenta con el respaldo de una sólida cartera de pedidos de clientes”. Ver más: La deuda de CoreWeave se desploma y reaviva los temores sobre una burbuja de la IA Desde luego, CoreWeave no fue la única afectada por la ola de ventas de esta semana. El índice de semiconductores de la Bolsa de Filadelfia, conocido por su símbolo SOX, ha caído un 9,7% esta semana, lo que supone un descenso del 22% respecto al máximo alcanzado en junio. Los fabricantes de servidores Dell Technologies Inc. ( DELL ) y Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. ( HPQ ) registraron fuertes caídas. Sin embargo, CoreWeave es considerada una de las acciones más arriesgadas del sector de la inteligencia artificial debido a su gran dependencia de la deuda de alto rendimiento para financiar sus centros de datos. La empresa obtuvo en marzo, por primera vez, calificaciones de grado de inversión para su deuda respaldada por chips, y el objetivo es seguir obteniendo calificaciones similares, según declaró este miércoles su cofundador Brannin McBee al Financial Times, lo que no hace sino subrayar la intención de CoreWeave de seguir recurriendo al crédito. La estrecha relación de la empresa con Nvidia podría constituir una fuente de capital si se restringiera su acceso al mercado, según el analista de Bloomberg Intelligence Robert Schiffman. No obstante, Huang rechazó dicha idea este jueves, afirmando que no hay necesidad de un rescate. “La solidez de CoreWeave mejora día a día”, declaró Huang a Bloomberg durante un acto celebrado en Estocolmo. “Soy optimista. De hecho, su coste de capital está disminuyendo”. Ver más: CoreWeave advierte sobre el costo y las dificultades que enfrentará si deja de usar chips de Nvidia Aun así, incluso con todos los riesgos que plantean el aumento de las tasas de interés y el nivel estratosférico del gasto en inteligencia artificial, el contexto fundamental sigue siendo alentador para CoreWeave, según Matt Bartolini, director global de estrategas de investigación de State Street Investment Management. “Todavía nos encontramos en una fase muy temprana del ciclo de inversión en IA, por lo que no creo que las tasas de interés vayan a suponer un obstáculo insuperable, pero sí que alteran el cálculo que subyace a la emisión continuada de deuda y a la garantía de que la financiación de dicha deuda pueda cubrirse con un crecimiento creíble en el futuro”, señaló Bartolini. “La tendencia de demanda a largo plazo es lo que está financiando el ciclo de inversión en capital, y creo que es probable que la demanda continúe independientemente de lo que ocurra con las tasas de interés”. -Con la colaboración de Subrat Patnaik, David Watkins y Carmen Reinicke. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Nvidia confía en que el impacto económico de la IA calme el nerviosismo del mercado
item.description: El CEO de Nvidia sostiene que la IA transformará todos los sectores y países, mientras las acciones de semiconductores acumulan ocho sesiones consecutivas de caídas por las dudas sobre la sostenibilid ...
item.dc:creator: Ian King
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — El CEO de Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ), Jensen Huang, se mostró optimista ante la última caída de las acciones del sector de la inteligencia artificial en los mercados bursátiles y afirmó que las ventajas de esta tecnología pronto contrarrestarán las preocupaciones de los inversores. “Todo esto va a pasar, y la razón es muy sencilla”, declaró Huang a Emily Chang, de Bloomberg, durante un evento celebrado en Berlín. “Va a suponer una transformación. Va a tener un impacto muy positivo en todos y cada uno de los sectores y en todos y cada uno de los países. No hay duda de que seguirá adelante, y nos encontramos en los inicios de este proceso”. Estas declaraciones pusieron fin a una semana tumultuosa para las acciones de los fabricantes de chips y las empresas de infraestructura de IA. El índice de semiconductores de la Bolsa de Filadelfia, objeto de gran atención, lleva ya ocho días consecutivos de caídas, lo que supone la racha bajista más larga desde 2008. Ver más: CEO de Nvidia minimiza temores por la deuda de CoreWeave y sus acciones revierten pérdidas Por su parte, las acciones de Nvidia han caído durante siete de las últimas ocho sesiones. Los inversores han expresado su preocupación porque el gasto en IA no sea sostenible en un momento en el que los costes de financiación son más elevados. A pesar de ello, Huang se ha mantenido firme en sus previsiones optimistas sobre el mercado de la IA y su impacto en la economía en general. Espera que los beneficios derivados de las inversiones masivas en hardware acallen, en última instancia, el nerviosismo del mercado. “En cuanto a algunas de las noticias, se trata de noticias irregulares”, afirmó. “Las noticias, como saben, surgen constantemente, pero no alterarán los fundamentos”. Nvidia desempeña un papel fundamental en el desarrollo global de la infraestructura de inteligencia artificial. Es el mayor proveedor de aceleradores de IA, chips que se utilizan para desarrollar y ejecutar modelos. Además, ha ampliado su actividad a una amplia gama de productos relacionados de hardware, software y servicios. Ver más: Nvidia suspendería el suministro de chips a empresas que desarrollen IA insegura, dice Jensen Huang La última ola de ventas ha afectado especialmente a CoreWeave Inc. ( CRWV ), un proveedor de servicios de computación en la nube que cuenta con Nvidia como uno de sus principales patrocinadores.
